title: Come, Ye That Love the Lord
description: Come, Ye That Love the Lord in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 417 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Heavenly Joy on Earth”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come, ye that love the Lord, And let your joys be known; Join in a song with sweet ac-cord, And thus sur-round the throne.

lines: Come, ye that love the Lord,
And let your joys be known;
Join in a song with sweet accord,
The men of grace have found
From faith and hope may grow.
Before we reach the heavenly fields,

licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
